rationale: Start with a broad gradient at intermediate temperature to locate all 10 peaks and identify the critical pairs without risking a low-organic hold. The elution window will guide subsequent gradient trimming and selectivity tests.

Lengthen only the gradient to test whether the remaining critical pair responds to a shallower slope. The current last peak at 8.06 min leaves room to improve resolution before the time penalty begins.

The critical pair worsened with a shallower gradient, so test a steeper gradient instead. This should shorten the run and may improve that pair, while checking whether the neighboring pair retains sufficient resolution.

Changing slope alone has not resolved the remaining pair, so shift the starting organic fraction to test a different selectivity window. The longer gradient should help preserve spacing in the early cluster while checking for excessive compression of the first peaks.

Injection 5 reached the maximum CRF; now shorten the gradient by one step to seek a faster fully resolved method. Keep its starting composition and temperature fixed to isolate the effect on the two closest pairs.
Shorten the gradient one further step to locate the speed limit for this composition window. Injection 6 remains a fully resolved fallback if either early critical pair drops below R = 1.5.

Narrow the gradient window to give a slope between the fully resolved 10-minute method and the slightly under-resolved 8-minute method. The last peak previously eluted near 0.64 organic, so a final fraction of 0.85 should keep it within the gradient.

Test whether a modest temperature reduction restores spacing in the compressed early pair at phi0 = 0.20. The steeper endpoint keeps the run short while probing a nearby selectivity trade-off rather than the unfavorable low-temperature extreme.
